questions.q: What common habit do many productive artists and thinkers share?
a: Working at a set time of day that suits them
Working only when inspiration suddenly strikes
Avoiding any fixed routine or workspace
Switching between day and night schedules constantly
questions.why: Lesson 1 says successful people pick their best hours and concentrate work there.

questions.q: Why can a warm drink in a favorite spot help before work?
a: The brain links the ritual with getting into a working mood
Caffeine removes the need for sleep entirely
It raises intelligence for the rest of the day
It replaces the need for a consistent schedule
questions.why: Lesson 1 says such rituals act like a pre-work warm-up that signals the brain to focus.

questions.q: What did some authors do to find inspiration, according to lesson 2?
a: Take long walks in nature, then hurry home to create
Wait at their desks until ideas arrive on their own
Copy the routines of whichever writer sold most
Only write during the hours they felt happiest
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes writers walking until inspiration struck, then rushing home to work.

questions.q: What does the summary say about copying a famous artist's creative process?
a: There is no single right way, so find what works for you
Following their exact routine guarantees similar results
Only routines involving coffee have proven effective
Every writer should work in the morning like Mozart
questions.why: Lesson 2 stresses that no method is universally right and that your muse may differ.

questions.q: How can a partner or friend support creative work?
a: By handling daily chores so more time goes to the craft
By criticizing drafts before anyone else can read them
By choosing which projects the artist should abandon
By keeping the artist away from social contact
questions.why: Lesson 3 says loved ones ease the burden of mundane tasks and support mental well-being.
